messages.subject: Re: modify the label of the legend and respect the order of colors of legend and chart
parts:
Are these the objectives? Relabeling fill variable levels in legend and second, reordering sequence of legend levels. 

1. Relabeling (see Winston Chang's cookbook site: http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Legends_(ggplot2)/)
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(TEMP, aes(x=CiradMed, Nbre)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = Type), stat="identity", width = 0.7)
######################################
q=p +

facet_wrap(~ Annee,nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Tout type de publication",     #titre graphique
    y = "Pourcentage de publications",  #label axe y
    fill="Type de\npublications"  ) +       #titre legende
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size=8,colour="black",face="bold"),
    #label graduation axe x
    axis.title.x = element_blank())#suppression label axe x

q
q+ scale_fill_discrete(labels=c("A", "B", "C","E"))

2. Changing sequence of legend labels - Could be done by reordering factor levels of the fill variable. 
str(TEMP)
# tells us that the fill variable, Type, is chr
levels(as.factor(TEMP$Type))# gives the default alpha ordering of CL,FI,OCO,SL
#Two steps... 
# Convert Type to factor var
TEMP$Type=as.factor(TEMP$Type)
# Reordering factor levels to FI,CL,SL,OCO by specifying level numbers
TEMP$Type = factor(TEMP$Type,levels(TEMP$Type)[c(2,1,4,3)]) 
levels(TEMP$Type)# confirm the change

# Plot again

p <- ggplot(TEMP, aes(x=CiradMed, Nbre)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = Type), stat="identity", width = 0.7)
######################################
q=p +

facet_wrap(~ Annee,nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Tout type de publication",     #titre graphique
    y = "Pourcentage de publications",  #label axe y
    fill="Type de\npublications"  ) +       #titre legende
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size=8,colour="black",face="bold"),
    #label graduation axe x
    axis.title.x = element_blank())#suppression label axe x

q
q+ scale_fill_discrete(labels=c("B", "A", "E","C")) # Relabeling factor levels

Best,
Vivek

parts:
Michel,

Apologies for the delay in replying back. My earlier suggestion for just relabeling involved introducing scale_fill_discrete(labels=...) and reordering legend labels involved reordering the factor variables and then relabeling. A much more simpler and direct  approach for reordering of labels could involve using scale_fill_discrete(breaks=...,labels=...), as in the following.

1. Use your original data: TEMP
2. Relabeling only (Unchanged from earlier suggestion)
---------------------------
library(ggplot2)

p <- ggplot(TEMP, aes(x=CiradMed, Nbre)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = Type), stat="identity", width = 0.7)
######################################
q=p +

facet_wrap(~ Annee,nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Tout type de publication",     #titre graphique
    y = "Pourcentage de publications",  #label axe y
    fill="Type de\npublications"  ) +       #titre legende
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size=8,colour="black",face="bold"),
    #label graduation axe x
axis.title.x = element_blank())#suppression label axe x

q
q+ scale_fill_discrete(labels=c("A", "B", "C","E"))

-----------------------------------
3. Changing sequence of labels and relabeling
------------------------------------------------------------------
q+scale_fill_discrete(breaks=c("FI","CL","SL","OCO"),labels=c("B", "A", "E","C"))
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

Few links that helped me when I faced with a similar issue in the past:
http://www.cookbook-r.com/Graphs/Legends_(ggplot2)/
https://kohske.wordpress.com/2010/12/29/faq-how-to-order-the-factor-variables-in-ggplot2/
http://learnr.wordpress.com/2010/03/23/ggplot2-changing-the-default-order-of-legend-labels-and-stacking-of-data/
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9577680/r-sort-legend-in-ggplot2
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7556320/reorder-legend-without-changing-order-of-points-on-plot

Best,
Vivek

On Tuesday, March 11, 2014 12:25:57 PM UTC+1, Vivek wrote:
Michel,

Apologies for the delay in replying back. My earlier suggestion for just relabeling involved introducing scale_fill_discrete(labels=...) and reordering legend labels involved reordering the factor variables and then relabeling. A much more simpler and direct  approach for reordering of labels could involve using scale_fill_discrete(breaks=...,labels=...), as in the following.

1. Use your original data: TEMP
2. Relabeling only (Unchanged from earlier suggestion)
---------------------------
library(ggplot2)
p <- ggplot(TEMP, aes(x=CiradMed, Nbre)) +
  geom_bar(aes(fill = Type), stat="identity", width = 0.7)
######################################
q=p + 
  facet_wrap(~ Annee,nrow = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Tout type de publication",     #titre graphique
    y = "Pourcentage de publications",  #label axe y
    fill="Type de\npublications"  ) +       #titre legende
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(size=8,colour="black",face="bold"),
    #label graduation axe x
    axis.title.x = element_blank())#suppression label axe x
q
q+ scale_fill_discrete(labels=c("A", "B", "C","E"))
-----------------------------------
3. Changing sequence of labels and relabeling
------------------------------------------------------------------
q+scale_fill_discrete(breaks=c("FI","CL","SL","OCO"),labels=c("B", "A", "E","C"))
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------

http://learnr.wordpress.com/2010/03/23/ggplot2-changing-the-default-order-of-legend-labels-and-stacking-of-data/
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/9577680/r-sort-legend-in-ggplot2
http://stackoverflow.com/questions/7556320/reorder-legend-without-changing-order-of-points-on-plot
